title: Spatiotemporal imaging of microwave magnetic fields via magnonic coherent splitting
authors: C. K. Wei, Z. J. Chen, J. T. Song, S. H. Ma, W. H. Liu, J. H. Wu, Z. W. Huang, Jinwei Rao, Wei Lu, Bimu Yao
abstract: Spatiotemporal microwave magnetic-field imaging reveals current flow in high-frequency circuits and nonequilibrium spin dynamics, yet probes rarely combine calibrated spectral readout, optics-free operation and transient mapping at room temperature. Here ferrimagnetic order in yttrium iron garnet supports coherent coupling from a pump-induced magnon mode, converting target-field amplitude into a spectral splitting with all-microwave readout. Sampling the calibrated splitting over position and delay reconstructs spatiotemporal imaging of magnetic fields. Continuous-wave measurement reaches a sensitivity of 58 pT/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ and recovers phases across various powers. Combined with time-resolved frequency-comb spectroscopy, the method reconstructs transient fields with a 130-ns response time. Coplanar-waveguide imaging validates the magnetic selectivity of the mode-splitting readout, where measured maps agree with simulated magnetic-field distribution. In a microwave amplifier, our reconstruction resolves nonuniform switching dynamics and detects downstream field suppression from an open-contact fault. Magnonic coherent splitting provides a scalable route for optics-free imaging of spatiotemporal field evolution in functional devices.
summary: The authors present a novel, all-microwave technique using magnonic coherent splitting in YIG to image microwave magnetic fields. By measuring the spectral splitting between two magnon modes, they achieve high sensitivity and temporal resolution for mapping magnetic field distributions. This method proves valuable for non-destructive diagnostics of high-frequency circuits and spintronic devices.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a room-temperature, optics-free method for spatiotemporal imaging of microwave magnetic fields, which is crucial for diagnosing high-frequency circuits and studying nonequilibrium spin dynamics.
main_result: The technique successfully reconstructs microwave magnetic fields across position and time, demonstrating high sensitivity (58 pT/sqrt(Hz)) and resolving dynamic events like switching and faults in RF amplifiers.
method: The method utilizes magnonic coherent splitting in YIG, where the target magnetic field amplitude is transduced into a measurable spectral splitting via coupling between a pump-induced magnon mode and a Walker mode.
model_or_system: The physical system is Yttrium iron garnet (YIG) exhibiting ferrimagnetic order. The mechanism relies on the coherent coupling between a pump-induced magnon mode (PIM) and a Walker mode (WM), providing a calibrated relationship between the field and the spectral splitting.
key_observables: Spectral splitting magnitude (related to field amplitude $B$), phase ($\phi$), and time-resolved field evolution $B(r, 	au)$.
important_parameters: Sensitivity of 58 pT/sqrt(Hz); time resolution of 130-ns; operating at room temperature.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the PIM–WM coupling strength provides a reliable, calibrated link to the magnetic field amplitude $B$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the field-to-splitting transduction mechanism, calibration curves showing $g(B)$ vs. $B$, and protocols for both spatial and time-resolved imaging.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical basis of the coherent splitting, presents the experimental setup for spatial and temporal mapping, validates the magnetic selectivity against electric field measurements, and applies the technique to diagnose faults in an RF amplifier.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates a novel, all-microwave sensing modality for magnetic fields in functional devices, providing a powerful tool for characterizing high-frequency dynamics without relying on optics.
